transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2027-03-12
- Time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~48 minutes (recorded)
- Attendees: Marcus Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nandi (Redwood SE), Oliver Chen (Redwood CSM); Sofia Martinez (Arbor Head of Platform), Ethan Park (SRE), Lina Holt (Procurement), Dr. Omar Farouk (ML Lead)

Summary: quick renewal check-in focused on Arbor's upcoming contract renewal in May, discussion about bumping committed capacity, adding eu-west and eu-central regions, and exploring a short Dedicated pilot for high-throughput inference. Procurement timelines surfaced and Redwood to provide pricing and runbook.

Topics: renewal timing; committed capacity tiers; Dedicated vs hosted for peak load; region activation timeline (eu-west-1, eu-central-1); security artifacts and SOC2/ISO audit questions; pilot scope and benchmark plan.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Marcus Lee: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we're keeping this short today, wanted to run through your renewal timeline and the region ask — Sofia, do you want to kick off with where you are on priorities?
[00:18] Sofia Martinez: yeah sure, thanks Marcus. basically we're coming into the last 60 days of our current term, and the main ask from the product org is to add eu-west and eu-central, we also have a two x spike expected q3, so we need committed capacity planning. procurement and finance want visibility on pricing and PO timings.
[00:36] Ethan Park: and on top of that we have some latency SLAs for EU traffic, 99th percentile needs to be under 220ms for our core inference path, so that is the hard constraint.
[00:48] Priya Nandi: ok good, so the options we typically discuss are bumping committed units on Hosted API vs provisioning Dedicated pools in those regions. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation; hosted is faster to spin up but you might see variable tail latency during global peaks.
[01:05] Dr. Omar Farouk: quick question on the Dedicated option — is there an on-prem or VPC option if we need complete data residency later?
[01:10] Priya Nandi: yes, Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem packaging, but that's a heavier lift and usually a separate contract. for now Dedicated in eu-west should meet your residency and isolation needs without moving fully on-prem.
[01:24] Sofia Martinez: that's what we were thinking. one other thing: we use long context prompts a lot — conversation + user history — so KV cache behavior and memory footprint matters. any notes on model variants or quant profiles you recommend?
[01:38] Priya Nandi: right, great point. our Optimize team generally recommends medium-quant profiles for long-context models to balance perf and token cost; also prefix caching for common system prompts helps. i'll share the profiling doc, but in short: for 8k-ish contexts we recommend a Dedicated 2-gpu pool per region as a baseline and then autoscale.
[01:56] Ethan Park: 2-GPU pool sounds fine but can you share an expected tokens/sec/ per-GPU number? we need to compare to our throughput baseline.
[02:04] Priya Nandi: yes — i'll pull a recent benchmark, but ballpark 400-600 tokens/sec per A100-equivalent GPU with batching tuned to your prompt length distribution; i'll put exact CSVs in the runbook.
[02:16] Lina Holt: from procurement perspective we need to know the billing cadence if we move to Dedicated and whether committed capacity can be split across regions on the invoice. also SLAs — what's the uplift for enterprise SLA vs standard?
[02:30] Oliver Chen: billing can be consolidated. we support per-account invoicing with region tags. enterprise SLA packages bump uptime/latency guarantees and include faster support SLAs — we can include that in the quote.
[02:42] Sofia Martinez: security — we need SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 docs, plus KMS integration details and audit log retention. do you have those artifacts ready to share?
[02:53] Marcus Lee: absolutely — i'll send the security pack and our SOC2 attestation link after the call. Priya, can you add the KMS integration note?
[03:00] Priya Nandi: yes i'll attach the KMS/HSM integration guide and the audit log retention options — default is 90 days in the console, enterprise retention can be extended.
[03:10] Dr. Omar Farouk: and on fallbacks — if eu capacity spikes, can requests be routed to another region gracefully or is that a hard fail?
[03:18] Priya Nandi: we have smart routing — policy based. you can set prefer-local with fallback to global-hosted variant; latency-aware routing will attempt local first, then failover. scoping that in the pilot will be important.
[03:30] Ethan Park: we also want to run an A/B of model variants — lower-latency quantized vs full-fidelity — to measure quality regression. can Redwood support canary routing?
[03:39] Marcus Lee: yes, rollouts/canary are supported in the Console, and we can configure traffic splits per route. we'll help define canary metrics and tie into your eval prompts.
[03:48] Lina Holt: timeline wise procurement needs a finalized SOW end of next week if we're going to lock rates before April billing cycle, is that feasible?
[03:57] Marcus Lee: it's tight but doable — we'll prioritize the pricing scenarios. i'll create a two-tier commit proposal: baseline committed units + optional burst/dedicated add-on for eu regions.
[04:10] Sofia Martinez: excellent. one small note — our legal asked about data deletion and retention policies after contract end, can we get a clause example?
[04:18] Oliver Chen: yes we have standard data handling and deletion clauses, i'll include redlined examples.
[04:25] Priya Nandi: to make the pilot concrete, propose we spin up a dedicated 2-GPU pool in eu-west-1 for a week, run your production-ish traffic replay, capture 99p/median latency and cost per 1M tokens, and validate routing and canary behavior.
[04:42] Ethan Park: that plan sounds good. when can we start the replay?
[04:45] Marcus Lee: aiming for 2027-03-22 as a start date, we'll need a short data/data replay snippet from you and an estimate of qps to model.
[04:54] Dr. Omar Farouk: i can prepare a 48-hour sample.
[04:57] Lina Holt: i'll confirm PO cut-off but target date for internal approval is 2027-03-18.
[05:03] Marcus Lee: great. i'll recap after the call with links — pricing spreadsheet, runbook, SOC2 pack, and a short pilot checklist.

Recap / agreed next steps:
- Redwood to send pricing scenarios and a SKU map for Hosted vs Dedicated by 2027-03-15 (Marcus)
- SE to share Dedicated runbook, latency CSVs, and KMS guide (Priya)
- Customer to provide qps distribution and 48-hr replay snippet (Ethan / Omar)
- Procurement PO timing confirmation (Lina)
- Pilot target start date 2027-03-22

References shared during call:
- Pricing scenario spreadsheet (link - will be emailed)

End of transcript.
